title: donoteat this BONUS EPISODE 2: KILLDOZER!
premise: The presenter challenges the viral folk-hero account of Marvin Heemeyer through Granby’s property, planning and sewer disputes. He traces the offers of accommodation and sewer-connection requirements that preceded the destructive rampage, disputing the story of a ruined business cut off from the road.
coverage: The viral Heemeyer story, Granby’s land and sewer disputes, the armored rampage and the sanitation lesson, through the credits. The game town illustrates the geography; archival news footage shows the destruction. Historical claims and judgments about motives are the presenter’s account.

panels.heading: Patron bonus and personal introduction
panels.description: Cities: Skylines editor lays a curved dirt-road loop beside a paved road as the presenter explains the paid/pirated bonus and delayed production.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Road previews appear and completed segments extend the loop.

panels.heading: Never meet your heroes
panels.description: The game view widens to the road loop and sparse buildings; the presenter announces the popular-demand Killdozer episode.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Road-building continues; no Killdozer action is depicted.

panels.heading: The viral folk-hero account
panels.description: A Facebook screenshot by Tyler Macfarlane replaces the game, introducing a reasonable man driven to unreasonable action.
panels.camera: Cut from game to screenshot; the screenshot shows its vertical crop shifting.
panels.action: The screenshot scroll/crop progressively exposes later paragraphs.
panels.notes: The Facebook post dates the rampage to 2004. The presenter challenges its folk-hero account.

panels.heading: Access-road claim versus corrections
panels.description: The same Facebook account is shown while narration rates its muffler-shop, access-road and petition assertions.
panels.camera: Screenshot shifts vertically.
panels.action: Later paragraphs move into the visible crop.
panels.notes: The presenter calls the blocked-road claim incorrect; the geographical comparison follows later.

panels.heading: Sewer claim establishes the real subject
panels.description: The screenshot exposes the claim that construction disconnected sewage service; the presenter calls that very incorrect.
panels.camera: Vertical screenshot reframing, not live footage.
panels.action: Text continues to be revealed.
panels.notes: The disputed sewer claim leads into the sanitation explanation.

panels.heading: Armor and entombment myths
panels.description: Later Facebook paragraphs celebrate the armored vehicle; narration disputes thickness and permanent entombment.
panels.camera: Progressive vertical screenshot crop.
panels.action: Still screenshot moves through its text.

panels.heading: The myth completes its rampage
panels.description: The lower post and attached Killdozer photograph appear as the quoted account celebrates buildings destroyed and a folk hero.
panels.camera: The screenshot’s vertical crop shifts down the post.
panels.action: Lower text and attached photograph enter view.

panels.heading: Rejecting the heroic version
panels.description: The bottom of the Facebook post shows the photograph, all-caps Killdozer Day salute and reaction counts.
panels.camera: Static screenshot crop before a cut back to game.
panels.action: No live vehicle motion; attached image is a photograph.

panels.heading: Patrick Brower is the source
panels.description: Killdozer book cover by Patrick Brower overlays the forested game editor.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: The cover is static while the background game view changes.
panels.notes: The presenter identifies Patrick Brower as a local reporter and one of Heemeyer’s perceived targets.

panels.heading: Not sponsored, just good
panels.description: Large white overlay reads I AM NOT SPONSORED BY THIS BOOK / I JUST THINK IT IS GOOD over the editor.
panels.camera: Cut/overlay over changing game view.
panels.action: Static disclaimer text.
panels.visualGag: The earnest book recommendation is punctured by an oversized non-sponsorship disclaimer; connected to the preceding cover/recommendation.

panels.heading: Granby relative to Denver
panels.description: Satellite map labels Granby and Denver in red with a connecting arrow.
panels.camera: Static map insert.
panels.action: Handwritten labels/arrow, no human action.
panels.notes: The map names Granby.

panels.heading: A small auto-oriented town
panels.description: Granby aerial map gains red street lines, a Route 40 line, circles and arrows for the town layout.
panels.camera: The map stays fixed while drawn annotations are added.
panels.action: Annotations point out streets, station, housing and city hall.

panels.heading: Zero Street and the two-dimensional model
panels.description: The map gives way to the game editor with the modeled railway station, tracks and street grid; narrator corrects the numbered-street count and remarks on Zero Street.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: The editor shows the town reconstruction from changing viewpoints.
panels.visualGag: The narrator’s surprise at Zero Street interrupts the town survey. His next admission, that he left out the hills, makes the reconstruction less grand.

panels.heading: Introducing Heemeyer with a portrait
panels.description: A close-up photograph of a smiling gray/white-haired, bearded man overlays the game editor and station during the introduction of Marvin Heemeyer.
panels.camera: Static portrait overlay.
panels.action: Still photograph; no live facial action.
panels.notes: The portrait accompanies Heemeyer’s introduction but has no identifying label.

panels.heading: The shop reconstructed without hills
panels.description: Game imagery returns to a dirt-road industrial yard bordered by trees, sheds and vehicles.
panels.camera: Changing angles and scale around the modeled yard.
panels.action: The editor presents the reconstructed industrial yard.
panels.visualGag: After surveying the town, the narrator admits the hills were more than he wanted to deal with. The flat game model gives away the shortcut.

panels.heading: Welder, property and Cody Docheff
panels.description: Game street grid alternates with a satellite locator; $42,000 IN 1992 and CODY DOCHEFF labels identify the auction and former owner.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Road/building editing and explanatory text overlays.

panels.heading: Locating the original shop
panels.description: Satellite inset outlines a small industrial parcel in red over the game model.
panels.camera: Cut to static annotated aerial inset.
panels.action: Parcel outline is static.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the poop pivot in the next panel: the supposedly heroic land dispute becomes a sewer-service story.

panels.heading: This story is about poop
panels.description: A large smiling poop emoji overlays the shop/editor view.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Emoji appears as a static overlay.
panels.visualGag: A giant smiling poop emoji replaces the heroic Killdozer story with a sewer problem. It returns when the dispute comes back to waste disposal.

panels.heading: What a proper septic tank would do
panels.description: Hand-drawn turquoise-and-brown cross-section labels SEPTIC TANK, POOP THAT FLOATS, POO GAS and CLEAN WATER TO LEECH; a sunglasses-wearing sun smiles above it.
panels.camera: The diagram holds on screen.
panels.action: The drawing shows how waste settles and water drains from the tank.
panels.visualGag: Blunt poop labels and a sunglasses-wearing sun turn the septic lesson into a cartoon. The same style returns for the blocked sewer and lift station.

panels.heading: A concrete truck barrel instead
panels.description: Brightly painted concrete mixer truck photograph appears over the editor.
panels.camera: Cut from cartoon diagram to static truck photograph.
panels.action: Photograph only.
panels.visualGag: After the proper septic-tank diagram, a concrete mixer illustrates the discarded truck barrel used to store sewage. The substitution makes the improvised system look absurd.

panels.heading: Concrete has a ticking clock
panels.description: Tall construction-site photograph showing many concrete delivery/pumping lines overlays the editor.
panels.camera: Static photographic insert over reframed game background.
panels.action: The construction-site photograph holds on screen.
panels.notes: The construction photograph illustrates hardened concrete loads and discarded drums, not this particular buried sewage tank.

panels.heading: Annexation and a private hookup
panels.description: Game shops and street grid return while narration explains a hundred feet of line and a lift station at the owner’s expense.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Building and road previews change; sewer construction is narrated, not visibly performed.

panels.heading: Gravity sewer setup
panels.description: Cartoon pipe slopes from a toilet to a main, labelled LATERAL, MAIN and POOP; the sunglasses sun returns.
panels.camera: Cut to static explanatory diagram.
panels.action: Drawn pipe topology.
panels.visualGag: Setup of the toilet-backup gag: cheerful crude drawing makes the engineering explanation concrete; same sun and poop vocabulary as the septic panel.
panels.notes: The narrator refers viewers to Franklin episode 6 for open-channel flow.

panels.heading: Poop gets stuck
panels.description: Diagram switches to an uphill pipe and the label POOP GETS STUCK.
panels.camera: Diagram changes.
panels.action: The pipe shape and label change.
panels.visualGag: Middle beat of gravity-flow gag: trying to send sewage uphill produces a blunt POOP GETS STUCK warning, leading to the toilet eruption.

panels.heading: Poop backs up
panels.description: The toilet sprouts a drawn fountain under POOP BACKS UP while the pipe is dark.
panels.camera: Cut/update within the static diagram sequence.
panels.action: Drawn spray depicts the backup; no filmed toilet.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the slope/stuck setup: the cartoon toilet sprays waste upward under an explicit label; the cheerful sunglasses sun remains indifferent.

panels.heading: Lift station resolves the cartoon failure
panels.description: Diagram adds a deep vertical wetwell, black pump/grinder and discharge pipe above the hill.
panels.camera: The diagram stays fixed as its labels change.
panels.action: Wetwell and PUMP/GRINDER annotations identify the mechanism.
panels.visualGag: The pump resolves the blocked-pipe and erupting-toilet sequence. The engineering gets practical again, but the poop labels and cool sun remain.

panels.heading: Seventy thousand dollars and cheaper alternatives
panels.description: The game editor resumes placing shop/parking elements while the presenter prices the required private sewer work and mentions a cheaper proper septic tank.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Parking and building assets are selected/placed.
panels.notes: The cost and district-practice claims are the presenter’s.

panels.heading: Normal hookup becomes conspiracy
panels.description: Industrial sheds and streets are edited while narration explains Heemeyer’s suspicion of sewer-board member Ron Thompson and his family excavation company.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: The game viewport and building selections change.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the Catholic/Irish-republican cutaway in the next panel: the narrator ends the perceived-conspiracy escalation with worst of all, Catholics.

panels.heading: Worst of all: CATHOLICS!
panels.description: Oversized white CATHOLICS! text appears across the industrial game-editor view.
panels.camera: Static text overlay on the editor.
panels.action: The CATHOLICS! caption appears over the editor.
panels.visualGag: The perceived sewer-board conspiracy culminates in a mock-horrified CATHOLICS! reveal. This sets up the immediately following masked armed-group cutaway and later Catholic/IRA callbacks.

panels.heading: Catholics: unrelated armed cutaway
panels.description: A black-and-white photograph of masked, armed people in an alley abruptly overlays the editor, with partly obscured figures behind the foreground group.
panels.camera: An abrupt photographic cutaway interrupts the game view, which then returns.
panels.action: Still photograph, not live armed action.

sound.text: The deadpan “unrelated” is followed by “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”) over the Catholic/Irish-republican cutaway.

panels.visualGag: The CATHOLICS! card cuts to masked, armed people as the narrator calls the image “unrelated.” The slogan makes the Irish-republican association obvious. An armed-woman photograph and an IRA graphic later repeat the joke.
panels.notes: The cutaways are a running joke, not an endorsement of the armed group. The people in the photographs are unidentified.

panels.heading: Extortion by government fiat
panels.description: Game returns; large quoted overlay reads EXTORTION BY GOVERNMENT FIAT as the sewer dispute is narrated.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Static quotation overlays the changing editor.
panels.visualGag: Sarcastic quotation frames an ordinary private hookup bill as grand governmental extortion; connected to the conspiracy/Catholic escalation.

panels.heading: Ignored hookup; 1997 concrete proposal
panels.description: The game industrial plot develops, 1997 appears, and a red-outlined aerial parcel returns.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Prop/building editing and static map inset.
panels.notes: The presenter says the board annexed the property and tolerated the missing connection before the plant proposal.

panels.heading: Batch plant, not cement kiln
panels.description: Game view carries a stacked WATER / CEMENT / AGGREGATE / ADMIXTURES list.
panels.camera: Changing editor viewport; static text list.
panels.action: Plant ingredients are listed, not shown mixing.

panels.heading: The rotary-kiln distinction
panels.description: Photograph of a large rotary kiln overlays the game.
panels.camera: Static comparison insert.
panels.action: The kiln photograph holds on screen.
panels.notes: The proposed enclosed batch plant is distinguished from the dustier outdoor kiln.

panels.heading: Joe Docheff negotiates: first price
panels.description: Aerial parcels are outlined in blue/red; game then displays $250,000.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Maps and text identify lots and asking price.
panels.visualGag: Setup for escalating asking-price series; ordinary negotiations become a moving target in the following two panels.

panels.heading: The price moves to $375,000
panels.description: Large $375,000 label overlays the game as the presenter describes Joe returning with the initially requested money.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Static price overlay.
panels.visualGag: First payoff to $250,000 setup: meeting the asking price immediately causes a higher demand; connects forward to $450,000.

panels.heading: The price moves again to $450,000
panels.description: Large $450,000 label overlays the same town-building context.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Static price overlay.
panels.visualGag: Second payoff of the escalating-price visual series: even an outside investor and $350,000 offer cannot stop the target moving.

panels.heading: Plan B uses subdivision land
panels.description: Satellite inset outlines a third, green parcel beside the blue/red parcels; a conventional map follows.
panels.camera: Cuts between static annotated aerial and map.
panels.action: Parcel outlines show alternatives.

panels.heading: Land swap and a new building demand
panels.description: Game camera closes on a READY 2 ROLL auto-shop asset in a dirt yard; trucks, trees and other props accumulate.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: The view shows dirt texture, trees and parked vehicles added around the shop.
panels.visualGag: Continuation of the moving-target negotiation motif: the proposed swap also gains a demand for a 4,000-square-foot building; model is illustrative, not literal historical shop branding.

panels.heading: NIMBY activist
panels.description: Large NIMBY ACTIVIST text appears over the shop yard, followed by a satellite circle around nearby housing.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Caption identifies the new activist role; housing map is static.
panels.visualGag: The increasingly demanding seller gets a mock job-title reveal, NIMBY ACTIVIST, connecting the land negotiation to his opposition campaign.

panels.heading: Illegal rezoning in scare quotes
panels.description: The cluttered auto-shop yard carries the quoted caption ILLEGAL REZONING.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Static ironic text over editor.
panels.visualGag: The scare-quoted illegal-rezoning complaint is undercut by narration that the site already had concrete zoning; it sets up the next explicit dust/noise quote over a muffler-shop yard.

panels.heading: A muffler shop fears dust and noise
panels.description: Quoted caption WHOSE DUST AND NOISE WOULD RUIN HIS BUSINESS fills the screen over the READY 2 ROLL shop yard, parked vehicles, equipment and dirt.
panels.camera: The caption stays fixed over the editor view.
panels.action: Caption overlays the modeled industrial yard; no historical owner is shown complaining.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to NIMBY ACTIVIST and ILLEGAL REZONING: the noisy/dirty nature of a muffler-repair shop undercuts its owner's dust/noise grievance, with the visibly industrial yard reinforcing the contrast.

panels.heading: Hearings and concessions
panels.description: Game shifts from shop yard to a Food Lion-like building and its parking lot while the presenter recounts rejected negotiations, hearings, suit, dust/noise controls and landscaping.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Parking elements and landscaping are edited.

panels.heading: Restarted approval; opposition ebbs
panels.description: Game street and lots gain shrubs, parked spaces and props as the presenter describes redoing legal procedure and Fay Rumsey’s letter.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Landscaping and asset placement change.

panels.heading: A corrupt town allows a shed
panels.description: Caption reads SCREWED OVER BY A CORRUPT AND DISHONEST TOWN over the game industrial yard; sheds and trailers then populate it.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Ironic quoted caption, then props added.
panels.visualGag: The enormous grievance language is juxtaposed with narration’s deliberately mundane offense: allowing a shed across from an auto shop; payoff to extortion and illegal-rezoning captions.

panels.heading: Construction proceeds despite lawsuit
panels.description: The game yard fills with warehouse, trailers, stacked yellow materials and trucks as the presenter describes the Docheffs accepting litigation risk.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: The view shows the illustrative industrial model gaining stock and vehicles.

panels.heading: Back to poop
panels.description: Smiling poop emoji returns over the warehouse yard.
panels.camera: Overlay on changing game view.
panels.action: Static emoji.
panels.visualGag: The smiling poop emoji returns as Joe’s proposed solution brings the supposedly grand dispute back to sewage.

panels.heading: More literally than that
panels.description: Large text reads LITERALLY / NO, MORE LITERALLY THAN THAT above the yard; aerial map subsequently traces a red watercourse arrow.
panels.camera: Caption overlay followed by static map insert.
panels.action: Drawn watercourse route, not filmed waste discharge.
panels.visualGag: “Up shit creek” becomes literal. The captions insist on actual sewage in the irrigation ditch, then the map traces the watercourse.

panels.heading: Neighbors complain; illegal line fails
panels.description: Game parking lots and street edges are edited while narration describes rain-dependent pumping and a rejected unauthorized neighbor hookup.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Parking/tree assets change; no historical pumping or trench-digging is visibly filmed.

panels.heading: Town compels a sanitary connection
panels.description: Game shrubs and roads continue changing as the presenter recounts July 2001 enforcement and leniency.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Tree/brush edits continue.
panels.visualGag: The narrator sarcastically calls the demand to stop dumping sewage “clearly unreasonable,” returning to Heemeyer’s earlier claims of extortion.

panels.heading: A free connection is rejected
panels.description: The game town model remains on screen as narration describes Joe’s free easement and construction offer, the hang-up and lost suit.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Background editing continues; the phone call is not visually reenacted.

panels.heading: The dozer was not needed for a road
panels.description: Full-screen photograph of armored bulldozer precedes map comparison.
panels.camera: Cut from editor to static photograph.
panels.action: Photographed vehicle does not move.

panels.heading: 1999 access-road evidence
panels.description: Black-and-white aerial map of the area overlays the model.
panels.camera: Static aerial insert.
panels.action: Map only.

panels.heading: 2005 access-road evidence
panels.description: Color aerial map replaces the black-and-white image, retaining the industrial streets/plots.
panels.camera: Cut between static maps, not camera motion.
panels.action: Map comparison only.

panels.heading: Successful sale, not financial ruin
panels.description: Game returns and displays $400,000 above its commercial grid.
panels.camera: Changing game viewpoint with static price label.
panels.action: Shop/tree/road editing continues.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the poverty/ruined-business myth: the $400,000 sale caption recalls $42,000 purchase and the earlier negotiation-price series.

panels.heading: Until he finished some work
panels.description: Large white quoted text FINISHED SOME WORK overlays the game town grid and commercial buildings.
panels.camera: Static quoted text overlay.
panels.action: Text overlay, not footage of welding or armor construction.
panels.visualGag: The leaseback’s innocent-sounding “finished some work” appears in scare quotes before the MK TANK reveal: Heemeyer has been secretly building an armored bulldozer.

panels.heading: Marv’s Komatsu tank
panels.description: Water-information view is followed by MK TANK / MARV’S KOMATSU TANK label.
panels.camera: Game overlay mode changes; viewport shifts.
panels.action: Tank name is written as static text.
panels.visualGag: Reveal/payoff to the preceding FINISHED SOME WORK scare-quote card: the innocuous leaseback work becomes Marv’s Komatsu tank, an armored bulldozer secretly built in the retained shop space.
panels.notes: The presenter says Heemeyer interpreted the failed bulldozer sale as a divine sign.

panels.heading: Armor and scale
panels.description: Side-view photograph of armored bulldozer among rubble includes standing people.
panels.camera: Cut to static photographic feature montage.
panels.action: Photograph only.

sound.text: Brahms’s Tragic Overture, Op. 81, performed by the Musopen Symphony, accompanies the feature montage.

panels.notes: Armor thickness is the presenter’s description, not a measurement from the photograph.

panels.heading: Weapons mounted inside
panels.description: An interior photograph shows a rifle and optic mounted through a metal opening. Other mounted weapons follow in the photographic sequence.
panels.camera: Cuts among static weapon photographs.
panels.action: No firing or weapon handling is shown.
panels.notes: Gun names and calibers remain uncertain; the presenter disclaims expertise.

panels.heading: Gun expertise disclaimer
panels.description: Black card reads DISCLAIMER: I DON’T KNOW MUCH ABOUT GUNS.
panels.camera: Cut to static black title card.
panels.action: Static disclaimer.
panels.visualGag: Abrupt self-deprecating caveat punctures the detailed weapons catalogue; connected to preceding weapon photographs.

panels.heading: Cameras and hatch
panels.description: Bulldozer photographs acquire red arrows pointing at features and top armor.
panels.camera: Cuts between static annotated photographs.
panels.action: Arrows change; vehicle and people are photographed, not moving.
panels.notes: The presenter argues there was a hatch and rejects the entombment story.

panels.heading: Cabin monitors
panels.description: Vertical interior photograph shows wires, equipment and a person looking into an opening.
panels.camera: Cut from exterior to static interior photograph.
panels.action: The person and cabin equipment appear in a still photograph.
panels.notes: The photograph illustrates the cabin interior; the presenter describes its monitors.

panels.heading: Visibility and cooling
panels.description: Side photograph of steel shell over yellow tracks, with red arrow pointing to a small opening.
panels.camera: Static annotated photograph.
panels.action: Arrow points to feature.
panels.notes: The presenter describes a porthole, visor and extra cooling; the photograph shows an opening and arrow.

panels.heading: Blade and ripper
panels.description: Exterior photograph’s large red arrow points to the dozer blade; next photograph provides another vehicle angle.
panels.camera: Cuts among static photographs.
panels.action: Arrow annotations only.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the air-conditioning non sequitur: utilitarian smashing/ripping catalogue abruptly culminates in domestic comfort.

panels.heading: It also had air conditioning
panels.description: Generic window air conditioner appears alone on black.
panels.camera: Abrupt cut from armored vehicle to isolated appliance photograph.
panels.action: Static appliance photograph.
panels.visualGag: The blade-and-ripper catalogue ends with an ordinary window air conditioner on black. Domestic comfort makes an incongruous final amenity for the armored bulldozer.

panels.heading: Poop bucket and old habits
panels.description: Game water/power information screens return over the modeled town.
panels.camera: The editor view changes position, scale and angle around the game town.
panels.action: Information mode and asset selections change.
panels.visualGag: The narrator returns to the bucket-and-ditch sewage story because the living quarters lacked water and sewers. “Old habits die hard” undercuts the preceding air-conditioning luxury.

panels.heading: Cannot do the rampage in the game
panels.description: Game water view cuts to CBS4 archival aerial footage labelled BREAKING NEWS / Granby / EARLIER, showing armored dozer moving near another yellow machine.
panels.camera: The game cuts to aerial news footage following the vehicles.
panels.action: The dozer travels along the roadway in the archival footage.
panels.notes: The narrator says he cannot recreate the rampage in Cities: Skylines.

panels.heading: Catholic Church target: armed callback
panels.description: Black-and-white still of an armed woman with another person behind her interrupts the news video.
panels.camera: The still photograph briefly interrupts the aerial news footage.
panels.action: Static photograph.

sound.text: “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”) returns after “unrelated” over the armed-woman photograph.

panels.visualGag: The Catholic Church target prompts another supposedly “unrelated” armed photograph. The Irish slogan repeats the masked-group joke and sets up the later IRA graphic.

panels.heading: Scraper confronts the dozer
panels.description: News aerial view shows long yellow scraper and armored dozer close together along street.
panels.camera: The aerial camera follows the vehicles along the street.
panels.action: Vehicles change relative position along the street.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the Docheff-name gag card in the next panel within a serious target-list narration.

panels.heading: Douche-eff
panels.description: Black title card reads DOUCHE-EFF.
panels.camera: Abrupt black-card cutaway.
panels.action: Static white text.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the target-list setup: narrator cites Heemeyer’s insulting spelling and dryly adds because of humor; card makes the juvenile nickname unmistakable.

panels.heading: Thirteen buildings and an attempted propane attack
panels.description: Aerial news footage returns, then shows armored dozer beside a red storefront with dust rising.
panels.camera: Cuts and aerial tracking; the footage shows approach and dust changes.
panels.action: Vehicle pushes into building edge; damage and dust follow.
panels.notes: The propane-tank attack is narrated; no propane field is identified in the footage.

panels.heading: Building parts are heavy
panels.description: Successive aerial frames show storefront collapse, debris and a thick dust cloud around the dozer.
panels.camera: Aerial camera follows/reframes vehicle.
panels.action: Wall/roof debris falls and dust expands as dozer moves through the structure.
panels.notes: The presenter credits reverse-911 evacuation and rejects the nonviolent-rampage story.

panels.heading: Targets and heavy-equipment resistance
panels.description: Edited aerial footage alternates road travel and a close view of rubble atop the armored shell.
panels.camera: Cuts between overhead street travel and closer vehicle detail.
panels.action: Dozer changes location; rubble rides on shell.
panels.notes: The targets and firing are the presenter’s account; gunfire is not visible.

panels.heading: Street trees blamed for lost business
panels.description: News footage follows dozer down Main Street near street trees and parked cars.
panels.camera: The aerial camera follows the vehicles along the street.
panels.action: Dozer travels beside tree-lined frontage.
panels.visualGag: The narrator recounts a restaurant owner blaming lost trade on street trees. That grievance sets up the small-business card and the joke about uprooting the trees as a favor.

panels.heading: Small business owners are insane people
panels.description: Black card reads SMALL BUSINESS OWNERS / ARE INSANE PEOPLE.
panels.camera: Abrupt cut from news footage to text.
panels.action: Static title card.
panels.visualGag: The black card delivers the narrator’s punchline to the restaurant-owner story. It returns as the first lesson at the end.

panels.heading: Doing a friend a favor by kill-dosing trees
panels.description: News footage returns to dozer pushing into frontage amid trees, rooflines and dust.
panels.camera: The aerial footage cuts to a closer view of the frontage.
panels.action: Vehicle pushes against frontage; dust/debris increase.
panels.visualGag: As the dozer pushes into the tree-lined frontage, the narrator calls the destruction a favor for the owner who blamed the trees. It pays off the grievance and small-business card.

panels.heading: Catholic target and explicit IRA callback
panels.description: Green-white-orange graphic reads IRISH REPUBLICAN / ARMY around a black rifle silhouette.
panels.camera: Abrupt static graphic insert.
panels.action: No live action.

sound.text: “Tiocfaidh ár lá” (“our day will come”) follows “Unrelated” a third time, now over the Irish Republican Army graphic.

panels.visualGag: The IRA graphic spells out the association in the earlier armed cutaways while the slogan returns. The narrator then jokes that God was not on Heemeyer’s side.

panels.heading: Campbell’s and the end of the mission
panels.description: Aerial footage shows dozer pressing into collapsing commercial roof/walls amid dust.
panels.camera: The aerial camera reframes the collapsing building around the dozer.
panels.action: Vehicle becomes surrounded/obscured by building debris.
panels.notes: The presenter says the dozer became stuck at Campbell’s, overheated and Heemeyer died by suicide. The footage does not show the interior events.

panels.heading: Getting inside; a hatch all along
panels.description: News footage shows the dozer beside a damaged building before the game model returns.
panels.camera: Aerial cuts followed by cut back to game.
panels.action: Exterior vehicle/debris footage, then model.
panels.visualGag: The narrator says arduous armor-cutting revealed a hatch all along, an ironic return to the opening entombment myth.

panels.heading: Instant folk-hero response
panels.description: Finished game model is toured from overhead down toward Main Street.
panels.camera: The view shows descent/reframing from high aerial to lower street-facing view.
panels.action: Traffic moves in the model; no historical callers appear.
panels.notes: The presenter recounts sympathetic calls during the destruction and letters to the newspaper.

panels.heading: Dozer Day sympathy versus the sanitation cause
panels.description: Game view jumps back overhead and shows rubble-like patches among modeled businesses.
panels.camera: Cut/reframe to overhead model and wider views.
panels.action: Model damage textures/props visible, not live demolition.
panels.visualGag: Narration’s grand folk-hero/festival story is reduced to wouldn’t let him dump poop in a creek; callback to emoji and literal-ditch sequence.

panels.heading: Accommodated, not ruined
panels.description: Game tour moves from wider town to the dirt-road industrial yard now containing a rubble patch where shop assets stood.
panels.camera: The view shows changing orbit/viewpoint around yard.
panels.action: Traffic moves through the model while the ruined yard remains unchanged.
panels.visualGag: The narrator returns to the 400,000-dollar sale and free sewer offer to dispute the opening story of a ruined business.

panels.heading: One asshole setup
panels.description: Black card reads IF YOU MEET AN ASSHOLE ONE DAY / YOU MET AN ASSHOLE.
panels.camera: Cut to static title card.
panels.action: Static text.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the dozen-assholes reversal on next card; prepares narrator’s final literal/metaphorical poop pun.
panels.notes: The cop-in-a-TV-show quotation’s show, character and original source remain unknown.

panels.heading: A dozen assholes payoff
panels.description: Black card reads IF YOU MEET A DOZEN ASSHOLES EVERYDAY / THEN YOU’RE THE ASSHOLE.
panels.camera: Cut to second static text card.
panels.action: Static text.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to preceding one-asshole setup: repetition reverses blame back onto the aggrieved protagonist; connected to final poop-all-over-everyone spoken line.

panels.heading: Literal and metaphorical poop
panels.description: Game panorama returns near the train station and town streets.
panels.camera: The view shows viewpoint changing over rail corridor.
panels.action: Train/traffic positions change in model.
panels.visualGag: The narrator ends the asshole-card sequence by saying Heemeyer eventually “pooped all over everyone” in more ways than one. The sewage story becomes a metaphor for the attack.

panels.heading: Lesson one callback
panels.description: Black card reads 1. ALMOST ALL SMALL BUSINESS / OWNERS ARE INSANE.
panels.camera: Cut to static lesson card.
panels.action: Static text.
panels.visualGag: The earlier small-business card returns as the narrator’s exaggerated first lesson.

panels.heading: Don’t shit where you eat expands
panels.description: Second black lesson card lists DON’T SHIT WHERE YOU EAT / OR WHERE YOU WORK / OR IN SOMEONE’S CREEK.
panels.camera: Text list expands.
panels.action: Additional lines appear.
panels.visualGag: Setup/payoff sequence turns a familiar metaphorical proverb into a literal site-by-site sanitation checklist; full version follows.

panels.heading: An inspected and approved system
panels.description: Expanded card adds illegal sewage tank and ultimately toilet with inspected and approved septic or sewerage system.
panels.camera: Static expanded list.
panels.action: Completed text card.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to abbreviated proverb: the comic overlong specificity resolves the entire septic/barrel/ditch/bucket narrative into a genuine public-health rule.

panels.heading: Piracy economics and one-dollar ask
panels.description: Round DNE GOOD FOR ONE FARE logo on black replaces the lesson card.
panels.camera: Static end-brand insert.
panels.action: Logo only.
panels.visualGag: Spoken commercial reverses the piracy premise from opening: more than four minutes seeking a pirated video at $15/hour costs more than the requested dollar; logo itself is branding, not an independent visual gag.

panels.heading: Thanks and patron credits
panels.description: My Patreons heading and three white name columns rise from bottom of black screen.
panels.camera: The composition stays fixed while the credits scroll upward.
panels.action: Credit text scrolls upward.

sound.text: The patron roll credits Brahms’s Tragic Overture, Op. 81, performed by the Musopen Symphony.

panels.heading: Long credit roll
panels.description: Three densely packed patron-name columns continue scrolling on black.
panels.camera: The patron names continue upward through the fixed frame.
panels.action: Patron names scroll.

panels.heading: Final DNE fare-token logo
panels.description: Credits clear and DNE fare-token logo returns centered on black.
panels.camera: Cut/fade transition between credits and static logo.
panels.action: Static ending logo.
